figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Illustration of unsupervised skill discovery methods. (a) MI is invariant to traveled distances. (b) The MI objective simply
seeks any mapping between Z and S, while LSD finds the largest (longest) possible mapping. (c) LSD maximizes the Euclidean
traveled distance, which can lead to simple or trivial behaviors. (d) Our CSD maximizes the traveled distance with respect to our learned
controllability-aware distance function that assigns larger values to harder-to-achieve state transitions. This leads to more complex skills
that can be useful for downstream tasks.
figure_candidates.notes: Four-part geometric conceptual comparison of MI/LSD/CSD: two radial skill sets, latent-to-state mapping, and contrasting gripper/object directional preferences.
